newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs lower.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs lower.

text.p: CME pork bellies closed down the 3.00-cent-per-lb daily limit in all contracts and hog futures closed lower.
Traders estimated there was a pool of 150 to 200 February pork belly contracts offered limit down at the close, with 10 contracts in March and May and small amounts in the others.

Pork bellies were pressured early by the futures' premium to cash prices and later by chart-based selling. Although it was too early to store bellies for February delivery, traders said the current premium of futures to cash would cover storage costs from now until February.
Also, analysts and traders expect Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town storage report to show an increase in stored supplies. The report is to be released at 1330 CDT Tuesday.

The monthly USDA cold storage report, to be released at 1400 CDT Tuesday, did not appear to be a factor in Monday's trading, traders said. Analysts estimate the report will show October 1 pork belly stocks from 11.9 million to 13.7 million lbs versus 6.255 million a year ago.
In hogs, added pressure was tied to forecasts for $0.50 lower cash hog prices Tuesday in reaction to the expected reduced slaughter levels and weak cash pork prices.

One packing company said it has been operating pork plants at reduced levels. This week it will run some plants at less than 40 hours and the rest at no more than 40, versus normal 48 hour operations. High hog prices and sluggish pork movement were blamed for the reduced operations.
Spokesmen for other pork packers had not returned telephone calls by Monday afternoon.
CME hogs closed down 0.900 cent to unchanged with October off 0.725 at 55.125 and December off 0.750 at 53.600 cents per lb. Pork bellies were off 3.00 cents in all contracts with February at 68.300.
